label: Initiative 1
t: 50% property tax exemption for primary homes
threshold: majority of all ballots cast in the general election (not just votes on the measure)
what: Exempts 50% of the assessed value of a qualifying owner-occupied primary residence (the dwelling) from property tax. Owners must have lived in Wyoming at least a year and in the home at least six months of the prior year, and file a sworn claim with the county assessor. The earliest tax year affected would be 2027.
y: Owner-occupied primary homes get a 50% assessed-value exemption.
n: Existing property tax rules and exemptions (including the 2025 25% exemption on the first $1M) stay.
fiscal: Official ballot estimate: state revenue falls about $92.6M in FY2028 and $95.9M in FY2029, continuing each year. This covers the state only; the larger loss to counties, cities, school districts and special districts was not estimated.
pro: BCR Initiatives (Brent Bien, Cheryl Aguiar, Rich Weber), Wyoming Republican Party
con: Vote NO on Initiative #1, Wyoming Education Association, Wyoming Taxpayers Association, Wyoming Hospital Association, Wyoming County Commissioners Association, Wyoming community colleges

cost.note: Upper bound: exempts 50% of the assessed value of the dwelling on an owner-occupied primary residence; the ballot title says it applies to the residential structure, so land value may not be exempt and the actual cut can be smaller. Interaction with the existing 25% exemption is not stated in the official estimate.

reasons.services: The official estimate shows about $93-96M a year less state revenue, and local governments, schools and special districts that rely on property tax would also lose revenue.
reasons.fiscal: State revenue falls about $92.6M in FY2028 and $95.9M in FY2029 with no replacement source, and local losses are unestimated.
